messages:
acme_platform: Hey team — our production service hit 429s exactly at midnight, but our long-lived websocket stayed connected. UI still showed 0 credits for ~6 minutes after midnight and API kept returning 429 even though the billing dashboard says refill happened. Any idea why?

emily_support: sorry you're running into this — can you confirm if clients were holding a streaming connection (websocket or long polling) across the refill boundary?

acme_platform: yes websocket persisted. we have keepalive pings every 30s. we only saw the refill in dashboard at 00:00:05 UTC, but our requests still get 429 until 00:06:10 when we restarted the client.

emily_support: thanks. can you share a short repro: client timezone, approx number tokens consumed right before midnight, and one example response header from the 429? e.g. X-RateLimit-Remaining, X-Request-ID if present

acme_platform: tz UTC. tokens before cutoff ~1.2M, so bucket drained. example header from failed call: `HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests`, `x-request-id: req_01F3YF8K`, `x-credits-remaining: 0`

emily_support: got it. one hypothesis: long-lived sessions with active prefix/KV cache can keep an inflight allocation or cached counter that doesn't refresh until connection renewal. i'm going to escalate to infra — cc @raj_engineer for runtime behavior around refill visibility for streaming sessions.

raj_engineer: putting context — there is a known edge where the token accounting mirror used by the websocket worker caches the tenant credit state for up to 300s to avoid thundering updates at rollover. normally that is invalidated after a refill event, but we recently observed a race where a transient network hiccup prevented the invalidation signal from reaching the worker. result: dashboard shows refill, but the worker continues returning 429 until cache TTL expires or worker restarts.

acme_platform: okay that matches our observed ~6 minutes. is there a recommended workaround for customers in the meantime?

emily_support: short term — restart the client to force a reconnect (you already did that). alternative: for Dedicated/private customers we can patch the worker config to reduce the cache TTL; for hosted customers we can issue an immediate worker invalidation for your org. i'll open a ticket and request the invalidation now.

billing-bot: Ticket created: SB-2026-1147 — requested org-level worker cache invalidation and manual audit of midnight refill event.

raj_engineer: i'll follow up with logs from the websocket worker showing missed invalidation signal and include exact TTL values. long-term fix: add a forced invalidation on refill + fallback to poll the control plane if invalidation ack not received in 10s.

emily_support: for transparency — root cause likely a missed invalidation during the refill window leading to stale credit view on streaming worker. mitigation steps we took: 1) manual invalidation for acme org, 2) add monitoring alert for invalidation failures, 3) engineering follow-up to change TTL and add ack fallback.

acme_platform: thanks, appreciate the quick action. can you confirm whether customer usage during that 6m was counted against next month's quota? we need to know billing impact.

billing-bot: Audit: usage between 00:00:00 and 00:06:10 shows 0 accepted tokens (requests rejected with 429). No retroactive consumption applied. No credits were consumed after refill until the reconnect.

emily_support: summary for you: 1) no extra billing, 2) we performed manual invalidation, 3) eng is rolling a patch to avoid recurrence. i'll leave this open until patch is deployed — keeping ticket SB-2026-1147 linked. feel free to DM for access to logs. :thumbsup:

acme_platform: great, closing on our side once we see patch. thanks everyone.
